prompt:
A desktop marketing landing page for White Sail Labs, an independent market research lab, rendered edge to edge at 1440 by 900 with crisp readable text, no browser window, device or desk around it. It shows the page mid-scroll, in its pinned step-by-step section.

The visitor is an investor, CEO or strategist deciding whether to request early access. White Sail Labs sells research as a subscription: applied AI engineers and business engineers build an always-on fleet of agents that keeps a living world model of every company; when a fact arrives, only the surprise travels along the value chain.

The page IS a synoptic pressure chart, edge to edge, fine navy isobars under everything, zoomed in close. A slim navy band at the top carries a cream sail silhouette with three short speed lines beside the wordmark White Sail Labs, the navigation Who we are, Capabilities, Careers, Contact, and a Request early access button.

What leads is NVIDIA's station, very large at the centre right, turned over like a card to show its back: "NVIDIA · GPU shipments forecast +3.2% · updated 09:42 · caused by SK hynix HBM guidance via elasticity 0.4" and a small line chart titled "Forecast record vs consensus", tagged Illustrative. A thick gold front with semicircles enters from the left edge, carrying the surprise from SK hynix; thinner gold fronts leave off the right edge toward Microsoft and Meta, half out of frame.

Down the left side, a numbered step rail tells the sequence: "1 Signal · SK hynix guides HBM output +20%, model expected +12%", "2 Only the surprise travels · +8 pts", "3 NVIDIA · shipments forecast +3.2%" highlighted as the current step, "4 Customers and competitors". Under the rail, the headline "Your decisions. Better informed." and Request early access.

Visual law: crisp off-white chart ground, deep navy and warm gold as the only two inks, no red; station plots, front symbols and the step rail as the signature; labels in a clear technical grotesk. One dominant move: the giant turned-over NVIDIA station.
note: The render drew Microsoft and Meta brand logos and its own figures; neither ships.
